title: Parameterized SQLite Query
description: Safely query a database using placeholders.
code:
import sqlite3
conn=sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.execute('CREATE TABLE users(name TEXT)')
conn.execute('INSERT INTO users VALUES (?)', ('alice',))
name=input('Name: ')
print(conn.execute('SELECT name FROM users WHERE name=?',(name,)).fetchall())

title: Flask Security Headers
description: Add baseline security headers to your own Flask application.
code:
from flask import Flask
app=Flask(__name__)
@app.after_request
def headers(r):
 r.headers['X-Content-Type-Options']='nosniff'
 r.headers['X-Frame-Options']='DENY'
 r.headers['Referrer-Policy']='strict-origin-when-cross-origin'
 r.headers['Content-Security-Policy']="default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'"
 return r

title: Prevent Open Redirects
description: Allow only local absolute paths for redirects.
code:
from urllib.parse import urlparse
def safe_path(value):
 p=urlparse(value)
 if p.scheme or p.netloc or not value.startswith('/') or value.startswith('//'): return '/'
 return value
print(safe_path('/dashboard'))

title: Local Login Failure Counter
description: Demonstrate a local in-memory failed-login counter; production needs shared storage and careful lockout design.
code:
from collections import defaultdict
failures=defaultdict(int)
def failed(key):
 failures[key]+=1
 return failures[key]>=5
print(failed('training-user'))

title: Inspect Response Security Headers
description: Inspect headers on your own local practice application.
code:
import urllib.request
req=urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8000',method='GET')
with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=3) as r:
 for h in ['Content-Security-Policy','X-Content-Type-Options','X-Frame-Options','Strict-Transport-Security']:
  print(h,':',r.headers.get(h,'MISSING'))
